name: Warrant
comment: Grammar for the Warrant rule DSL, kept in sync with the parser (src/RuleSyntaxTree/Parsing). Cross-schema references are implemented: KEYWORD(<predicate> for <handle> [with <context map>]) — e.g. can(create_timesheet for users(@context user_id)) and check(is_open('p') for pay_periods(@context id) with k = @context v). A handle is a schema name, optionally row-bound with a single `(<arg>)` selector. Arguments may be literals, :name / ? bindings, @context <key>, or @column <schema>.<column> (a schema-qualified database column). If the DSL grows new tokens/keywords, add matching patterns here.

column-ref.comment: `@column <schema>.<column>` — a schema-qualified database column reference, resolved to a grammar-wrapped column at compile time. Highlights `@column`, then the schema key as a namespace and the column as a property (same line only).

schema-target.comment: `for <schema>` — both the header of a top-level `for <schema> { ... }` rule-set block and the `for <schema-handle>` inside a cross-schema can(...)/check(...). Highlights `for` as a keyword and the schema name that follows it as a namespace. Any optional row-binding `(@context id)` after the name is tokenized by the other rules. Same-line only (a match cannot span lines); when `for` and the name are on different lines, `for` falls back to the keyword rule below.

keywords.comment: The DSL's reserved words (Lexer::KEYWORDS). `can`/`check` also act as expression-position builtins for cross-schema references; they still scope as keywords here.
keywords.name: keyword.control.warrant

operators.comment: ! * ? operators, plus `=` for the assignment in a `with key = value` context-mapping clause.
operators.name: keyword.operator.warrant

punctuation.comment: ( ) , punctuation, plus { } delimiting a `for <schema> { ... }` rule-set block.
punctuation.name: punctuation.separator.warrant
